days.focus_note: The Lord's comfort and power begin here: 'Comfort ye my people' opens a new tone in Isaiah's prophecies. Chapter 40 speaks of preparing 'the way of the Lord,' God's incomparable greatness compared to nations and idols, and the promise that those who wait on the Lord 'shall renew their strength ... mount up with wings as eagles' (40:31). Chapter 41 continues with the Lord's reassurance to Israel, 'Fear thou not; for I am with thee' (41:10), and His call of His servant.
days.source_excerpt: “Comfort” is the first word of Isaiah chapter 40. It marks the beginning of a different tone... Isaiah 40:3–5: I can help prepare 'the way of the Lord.' ... 40:11, 29–31 ... 41:10–13, 17–18 ... Isaiah 40:3–8, 15–23; 42:15–16; 47:7–11 — God's power is greater than worldly power. Isaiah repeatedly reminded his people of God's matchless power, even compared to the oppressive worldly power that surrounded them. Isaiah 41:8–13; 42:6; 44:21. What has the Lord called you to do?

days.focus_note: The Lord's chosen servant is introduced (identified with Jesus Christ), bringing judgment and light to the Gentiles, opening blind eyes. Chapter 43 delivers the powerful message 'Fear not... I have redeemed thee' and Israel's role as the Lord's witnesses, that 'beside me there is no saviour' (43:11).
days.source_excerpt: These words can refer to Jesus Christ (see Isaiah 42:1–7)... 42:6–7. Isaiah's message to his people and to us is simple: 'Fear not' (Isaiah 43:1)... 'Return unto me,' He pleads, 'for I have redeemed thee' (Isaiah 44:22). Isaiah 43:10 — I can be a witness of the Lord. Isaiah 40:1–3, 9–11; 43:9–12. In what sense are you a witness of Jesus Christ? ... Jesus Christ has been charged with making the claim recorded in Isaiah 43:11.

days.focus_note: The Lord pours out His Spirit like water on dry ground, denounces idol worship, and declares Himself the only God ('I am the first, and I am the last; and beside me there is no God,' 44:6). Cyrus is named as the Lord's shepherd/anointed who will allow the Jews to rebuild Jerusalem and the temple.
days.source_excerpt: 44:1–4, 21–24 ... to King Cyrus, who allowed the Jewish people to return to Jerusalem and rebuild the temple (see Isaiah 44:26–28; 45:1–4). Isaiah 44:3–4; 45:8 — The Lord will 'pour' His blessings on me. After reading these verses, your children could water a plant and talk about blessings the Lord has poured out on them.

days.focus_note: Contrast between the false gods of Babylon (carried as burdens) and the true God who carries His people 'even to your old age' (46:4). Chapter 47 is a direct pronouncement of judgment against Babylon, Israel's captor, reminding them that worldly power will fall.
days.source_excerpt: 46:3–4 ... note that chapter 47 is addressed to Israel's captor, Babylon. What do these passages teach you about worldly things? What do they teach you about God? Ponder why this message might have been valuable to Jewish people in captivity.

days.focus_note: The Lord recounts His foreknowledge and His refining of Israel 'in the furnace of affliction' (48:10), and pleads for obedience, promising that peace would have flowed 'as a river' and righteousness 'as the waves of the sea' if they had hearkened to His commandments.
days.source_excerpt: Isaiah 48:10; 49:13–16 — The Lord can refine me through my afflictions. As you read Isaiah 48:10, ponder your own 'furnace of affliction.' ... By obeying the Lord, we can have 'peace … as a river' (Isaiah 48:18). Isaiah 48:17–18 — Keeping God's commandments brings peace.

days.focus_note: The Lord's servant is prepared even before birth for a mission to Israel and the Gentiles as 'a light' to them. Though efforts may seem 'for nought, and in vain' (49:4), the Lord assures His people He can never forget them, comparing His remembrance to a mother who cannot forget her nursing child.
days.source_excerpt: 49:7–16 ... Isaiah 49:1–9. What messages do you find in these verses that can help when your efforts and service seem to be 'for nought, and in vain'? (verse 4). Isaiah 49:14–16 — The Lord will never forget me. As you read verse 14, you could talk about what might make people feel forgotten or forsaken... According to Isaiah 49:15–16, why will the Lord never forget us?
